briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Turns Political as Michigan Operators Adapt — While DC Pushes Cannabis and Psilocybin Toward the Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax is now a full-blown governor's race issue, with both parties' front-runners pledging relief, even as savvy operators find new margins through cost-sharing deals, hospitality concepts, and cross-border traffic. Nationally, the DEA rescheduling hearing is in its closing stretch, Compass Pathways just banked a major psilocybin data win, and MSOs are consolidating fast — all signs the industry's next chapter is arriving ahead of schedule.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a cannabis tax-relief plank of his 'Freedom Agenda,' pledging to repeal or sharply cut Michigan's 24% wholesale tax and slash the retail excise tax from 10% to 5% — giving operators a real electoral path to relief in November.

Rize, which runs three Upper Peninsula stores, is proving the tax is survivable — the chain kept growing by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers rather than absorbing the 24% hit alone, even as rival Higher Love closed five of its nine U.P. locations.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is pushing the retail model forward, building a fully integrated cannabis hospitality concept — dispensary, on-site consumption, dining and event licensing under one roof — with a fall opening on deck.

Jars Cannabis notched a win in Madison Heights, negotiating removal of a police-monitored surveillance camera pointed at its parking lot after mounting a sign to block its view — a small but telling sign operators can push back on onerous local conditions.

Statewide license attrition remains real — active retail licenses slipped from 845 to 836 year-over-year — but a bipartisan repeal bill for the 24% tax is now on the table in Lansing alongside fresh momentum from both governor's-race camps, giving operators a clearer legislative target for relief.

national.text: The DEA's cannabis rescheduling hearing is in its final stretch, with the agency filing its closing case arguing cannabis has currently accepted medical use — a key legal threshold for the Schedule III move — while opposition briefs from SAM and allied states largely rehash prior arguments rather than break new ground.

The rescheduling process cleared a procedural milestone in mid-August, with a formal rule proposal expected before year-end 2026; Schedule III would eliminate the crushing 280E tax penalty, potentially cutting effective operator tax rates from roughly 60% to the mid-20s.

Compass Pathways was named a 2026 Fierce 50 Breakthrough honoree just days after six-month data from its second Phase 3 trial confirmed COMP360 psilocybin's rapid, durable effect on treatment-resistant depression, keeping the company on track for FDA filing and a possible approval before 2027.

The FDA has scheduled a public hearing for September 14 on psychedelic medicine policy, part of what's been the government's most significant coordinated push on psychedelics in decades — including executive action, expedited review vouchers for Compass, Usona and Transcend, and new research funding.

Consolidation is accelerating in operators' favor: Cresco Labs picked up nine Pennsylvania medical dispensaries for $50 million from a distressed PharmaCann, part of a broader wave of well-capitalized MSOs snapping up assets in mature, limited-license markets.
